L.7n3: ^107:2^ My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and will give praise, with my glory.
L.7n5: ^107:3^ Arise, my glory; arise, psaltery and harp * I will arise in the morning early.
L.7n8: ^107:4^ I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: * and I will sing unto thee among the nations.
L.7n9: ^107:5^ For thy mercy is great above the heavens: * and thy truth even unto the clouds.
L.7nb: ^107:6^ Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory over all the earth: * that thy beloved may be delivered.
L.7ne: ^107:7^ Save with thy right hand and hear me. * God hath spoken in his holiness.
L.7ng: ^107:8^ I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem * and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles.
L.7nh: ^107:9^ Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim the protection of my head.
L.7ms: ^107:10^ Juda is my king: * Moab the pot of my hope.
L.7mu: ^107:10^ Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe: * the aliens are become my friends.
L.7mw: ^107:11^ Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?
L.7my: ^107:12^ Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies?
L.7n0: ^107:13^ O grant us help from trouble: * for vain is the help of man.
L.7n2: ^107:14^ Through God we shall do mightily: * and he will bring our enemies to nothing.
L.7on: ^108:2^ Deus, laudem meam ne tacúeris: * quia os peccatóris, et os dolósi super me apértum est.
L.7ot: ^108:3^ Locúti sunt advérsum me lingua dolósa, et sermónibus ódii circumdedérunt me: * et expugnavérunt me gratis.
L.7ow: ^108:4^ Pro eo ut me dilígerent, detrahébant mihi: * ego autem orábam.
L.7oy: ^108:5^ Et posuérunt advérsum me mala pro bonis: * et ódium pro dilectióne mea.
L.7oz: ^108:6^ Constítue super eum peccatórem: * et diábolus stet a dextris ejus.
L.7p1: ^108:7^ Cum judicátur, éxeat condemnátus: * et orátio ejus fiat in peccátum.
L.7p3: ^108:8^ Fiant dies ejus pauci: * et episcopátum ejus accípiat alter.
L.7p5: ^108:9^ Fiant fílii ejus órphani: * et uxor ejus vídua.
L.7nk: ^108:10^ Nutántes transferántur fílii ejus, et mendícent: * et eiciántur de habitatiónibus suis.
L.7nm: ^108:11^ Scrutétur fænerátor omnem substántiam ejus: * et dirípiant aliéni labóres ejus.
L.7no: ^108:12^ Non sit illi adjútor: * nec sit qui misereátur pupíllis ejus.
L.7np: ^108:13^ Fiant nati ejus in intéritum: * in generatióne una deleátur nomen ejus.
L.7nr: ^108:14^ In memóriam rédeat iníquitas patrum ejus in conspéctu Dómini: * et peccátum matris ejus non deleátur.
L.7nt: ^108:15^ Fiant contra Dóminum semper, et dispéreat de terra memória eórum: * pro eo quod non est recordátus fácere misericórdiam.
L.7nw: ^108:17^ Et persecútus est hóminem ínopem, et mendícum, * et compúnctum corde mortificáre.
L.7nz: ^108:18^ Et diléxit maledictiónem, et véniet ei: * et nóluit benedictiónem, et elongábitur ab eo.
L.7o0: ^108:18^ Et índuit maledictiónem sicut vestiméntum, * et intrávit sicut aqua in interióra ejus, et sicut óleum in óssibus ejus.
L.7o1: ^108:19^ Fiat ei sicut vestiméntum, quo operítur: * et sicut zona, qua semper præcíngitur.
L.7o3: ^108:20^ Hoc opus eórum, qui détrahunt mihi apud Dóminum: * et qui loquúntur mala advérsus ánimam meam.
L.7o6: ^108:21^ Et tu, Dómine, Dómine, fac mecum propter nomen tuum: * quia suávis est misericórdia tua.
L.7o8: ^108:22^ Líbera me quia egénus, et pauper ego sum: * et cor meum conturbátum est intra me.
L.7oa: ^108:23^ Sicut umbra cum declínat, ablátus sum: * et excússus sum sicut locústæ.
L.7ob: ^108:24^ Génua mea infirmáta sunt a jejúnio: * et caro mea immutáta est propter óleum.
L.7oe: ^108:25^ Et ego factus sum oppróbrium illis: * vidérunt me, et movérunt cápita sua.
L.7og: ^108:26^ Ádjuva me, Dómine, Deus meus: * salvum me fac secúndum misericórdiam tuam.
L.7oi: ^108:27^ Et sciant quia manus tua hæc: * et tu, Dómine, fecísti eam.
L.7oj: ^108:28^ Maledícent illi, et tu benedíces: * qui insúrgunt in me, confundántur: servus autem tuus lætábitur.
L.7ol: ^108:29^ Induántur qui détrahunt mihi, pudóre: * et operiántur sicut diplóide confusióne sua.
L.7op: ^108:30^ Confitébor Dómino nimis in ore meo: * et in médio multórum laudábo eum.
L.7os: ^108:31^ Quia ástitit a dextris páuperis, * ut salvam fáceret a persequéntibus ánimam meam.
L.7oo: ^108:2^ God, be not thou silent in my praise: * for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful man is opened against me.
L.7ou: ^108:3^ They have spoken against me with deceitful tongues; and they have compassed me about with words of hatred; * and have fought against me without cause.
L.7ov: ^108:4^ Instead of making me a return of love, they detracted me: * but I gave myself to prayer.
L.7ox: ^108:5^ And they repaid me evil for good: * and hatred for my love.
L.7p0: ^108:6^ Set thou the sinner over him: * and may the devil stand at his right hand.
L.7p2: ^108:7^ When he is judged, may he go out condemned; * and may his prayer be turned to sin.
L.7p4: ^108:8^ May his days be few: * and his bishopric let another take.
L.7p6: ^108:9^ May his children be fatherless, * and his wife a widow.
L.7nj: ^108:10^ Let his children be carried about vagabonds, and beg; * and let them be cast out of their dwellings.
L.7nl: ^108:11^ May the usurer search all his substance: * and let strangers plunder his labours.
L.7nn: ^108:12^ May there be none to help him: * nor none to pity his fatherless offspring.
L.7nq: ^108:13^ May his posterity be cut off; * in one generation may his name be blotted out.
L.7ns: ^108:14^ May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered in the sight of the Lord: * and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.
L.7nu: ^108:15^ May they be before the Lord continually, and let the memory of them perish from the earth: * because he remembered not to shew mercy,
L.7nv: ^108:17^ But persecuted the poor man and the beggar; * and the broken in heart, to put him to death.
L.7nx: ^108:18^ And he loved cursing, and it shall come unto him: * and he would not have blessing, and it shall be far from him.
L.7ny: ^108:18^ And he put on cursing, like a garment: * and it went in like water into his entrails, and like oil in his bones.
L.7o2: ^108:19^ May it be unto him like a garment which covereth him; * and like a girdle with which he is girded continually.
L.7o4: ^108:20^ This is the work of them who detract me before the Lord; * and who speak evils against my soul.
L.7o5: ^108:21^ But thou, O Lord, do with me for thy name’s sake: * because thy mercy is sweet.
L.7o7: ^108:22^ Do thou deliver me, for I am poor and needy, * and my heart is troubled within me.
L.7o9: ^108:23^ I am taken away like the shadow when it declineth: * and I am shaken off as locusts.
L.7oc: ^108:24^ My knees are weakened through fasting: * and my flesh is changed for oil.
L.7od: ^108:25^ And I am become a reproach to them: * they saw me and they shaked their heads.
L.7of: ^108:26^ Help me, O Lord my God; * save me according to thy mercy.
L.7oh: ^108:27^ And let them know that this is thy hand: * and that thou, O Lord, hast done it.
L.7ok: ^108:28^ They will curse and thou wilt bless: * let them that rise up against me be confounded: but thy servant shall rejoice.
L.7om: ^108:29^ Let them that detract me be clothed with shame: * and let them be covered with their confusion as with a double cloak.
L.7oq: ^108:30^ I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth: * and in the midst of many I will praise him.
L.7or: ^108:31^ Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor, * to save my soul from persecutors.
L.8ge: ^38:2^ Dixi: Custódiam vias meas: * ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
L.8gh: ^38:2^ Pósui ori meo custódiam, * cum consísteret peccátor advérsum me.
L.8gj: ^38:3^ Obmútui, et humiliátus sum, et sílui a bonis: * et dolor meus renovátus est.
L.8gk: ^38:4^ Concáluit cor meum intra me: * et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis.
L.8gp: ^38:5^ Locútus sum in lingua mea: * Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
L.8gn: ^38:5^ Et númerum diérum meórum quis est: * ut sciam quid desit mihi.
L.8gs: ^38:6^ Ecce mensurábiles posuísti dies meos: * et substántia mea tamquam níhilum ante te.
L.8gt: ^38:6^ Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, * omnis homo vivens.
L.8gx: ^38:7^ Verúmtamen in imágine pertránsit homo: * sed et frustra conturbátur.
L.8gw: ^38:7^ Thesaurízat: * et ignórat cui congregábit ea.
L.8gz: ^38:8^ Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus? * Et substántia mea apud te est.
L.8h0: ^38:9^ Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me: * oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
L.8g3: ^38:10^ Obmútui, et non apérui os meum, quóniam tu fecísti: * ámove a me plagas tuas.
L.8g4: ^38:12^ A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus: * propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem.
L.8g6: ^38:12^ Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus: * verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo.
L.8g9: ^38:13^ Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
L.8gb: ^38:13^ Ne síleas: quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus, * sicut omnes patres mei.
L.8gd: ^38:14^ Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam, * et ámplius non ero.
L.8gg: ^38:2^ I said: I will take heed to my ways: * that I sin not with my tongue.
L.8gf: ^38:2^ I have set guard to my mouth, * when the sinner stood against me.
L.8gi: ^38:3^ I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: * and my sorrow was renewed.
L.8gl: ^38:4^ My heart grew hot within me: * and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.
L.8go: ^38:5^ I spoke with my tongue: * O Lord, make me know my end.
L.8gm: ^38:5^ And what is the number of my days: * that I may know what is wanting to me.
L.8gr: ^38:6^ Behold thou hast made my days measurable: * and my substance is as nothing before thee.
L.8gq: ^38:6^ And indeed all things are vanity: * every man living.
L.8gv: ^38:7^ Surely man passeth as an image: * yea, and he is disquieted in vain.
L.8gu: ^38:7^ He storeth up: * and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.
L.8gy: ^38:8^ And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? * And my substance is with thee.
L.8h1: ^38:9^ Deliver thou me from all my iniquities: * thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.
L.8g2: ^38:10^ I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because thou hast done it: * remove thy scourges from me.
L.8g7: ^38:12^ The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: * thou hast corrected man for iniquity.
L.8g5: ^38:12^ And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: * surely in vain is any man disquieted.
L.8ga: ^38:13^ Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: * give ear to my tears.
L.8g8: ^38:13^ Be not silent: for I am a stranger with thee, * and a sojourner as all my fathers were.
L.8gc: ^38:14^ O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, * and be no more.
L.8hz: ^40:2^ Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
L.8i1: ^40:3^ Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum ejus.
L.8i3: ^40:4^ Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris ejus: * univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus.
L.8i5: ^40:5^ Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
L.8i7: ^40:6^ Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
L.8ib: ^40:7^ Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor ejus congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
L.8ia: ^40:7^ Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
L.8id: ^40:8^ Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
L.8ig: ^40:9^ Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
L.8hq: ^40:10^ Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
L.8hs: ^40:11^ Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
L.8hu: ^40:12^ In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
L.8hw: ^40:13^ Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
L.8hx: ^40:14^ Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
L.8i0: ^40:2^ Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.
L.8i2: ^40:3^ The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.
L.8i4: ^40:4^ The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.
L.8i6: ^40:5^ I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.
L.8i8: ^40:6^ My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?
L.8i9: ^40:7^ And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.
L.8ic: ^40:7^ He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.
L.8ie: ^40:8^ All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.
L.8if: ^40:9^ They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?
L.8hp: ^40:10^ For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.
L.8hr: ^40:11^ But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.
L.8ht: ^40:12^ By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.
L.8hv: ^40:13^ But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.
L.8hy: ^40:14^ Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.
L.8jh: ^43:2^ Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
L.8ji: ^43:2^ Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
L.8jl: ^43:3^ Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
L.8jp: ^43:4^ Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
L.8jq: ^43:4^ Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
L.8js: ^43:5^ Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Jacob.
L.8jt: ^43:6^ In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
L.8jw: ^43:7^ Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
L.8jy: ^43:8^ Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
L.8jz: ^43:9^ In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
L.8ii: ^43:10^ Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
L.8ij: ^43:11^ Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
L.8il: ^43:12^ Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
L.8io: ^43:13^ Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
L.8ip: ^43:14^ Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
L.8ir: ^43:15^ Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
L.8iu: ^43:16^ Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
L.8iv: ^43:17^ A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
L.8iy: ^43:18^ Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
L.8j0: ^43:19^ Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
L.8j2: ^43:20^ Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
L.8j4: ^43:21^ Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
L.8j6: ^43:22^ Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
L.8j7: ^43:22^ Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
L.8ja: ^43:23^ Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
L.8jb: ^43:24^ Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
L.8je: ^43:25^ Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
L.8jg: ^43:26^ Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
L.8jk: ^43:2^ We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,
L.8jj: ^43:2^ The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.
L.8jm: ^43:3^ Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.
L.8jo: ^43:4^ For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.
L.8jn: ^43:4^ But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.
L.8jr: ^43:5^ Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.
L.8ju: ^43:6^ Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.
L.8jv: ^43:7^ For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.
L.8jx: ^43:8^ But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.
L.8k0: ^43:9^ In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.
L.8ih: ^43:10^ But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.
L.8ik: ^43:11^ Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.
L.8im: ^43:12^ Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.
L.8in: ^43:13^ Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.
L.8iq: ^43:14^ Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.
L.8is: ^43:15^ Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.
L.8it: ^43:16^ All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.
L.8iw: ^43:17^ At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.
L.8ix: ^43:18^ All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.
L.8iz: ^43:19^ And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.
L.8j1: ^43:20^ For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.
L.8j3: ^43:21^ If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:
L.8j8: ^43:22^ Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.
L.8j5: ^43:22^ Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
L.8j9: ^43:23^ Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.
L.8jc: ^43:24^ Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?
L.8jd: ^43:25^ For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.
L.8jf: ^43:26^ Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.
L.8kr: ^48:2^ Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
L.8ku: ^48:3^ Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
L.8kw: ^48:4^ Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
L.8ky: ^48:5^ Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
L.8kz: ^48:6^ Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
L.8l1: ^48:7^ Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
L.8l3: ^48:8^ Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
L.8l5: ^48:9^ Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
L.8k4: ^48:11^ Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
L.8k2: ^48:11^ Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
L.8k5: ^48:12^ Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
L.8k8: ^48:13^ Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
L.8k9: ^48:14^ Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
L.8kd: ^48:15^ Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
L.8kc: ^48:15^ Et dominabúntur eórum justi in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
L.8kg: ^48:16^ Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
L.8ki: ^48:17^ Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus ejus.
L.8kk: ^48:18^ Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória ejus.
L.8km: ^48:19^ Quia ánima ejus in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
L.8ko: ^48:20^ Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
L.8kp: ^48:21^ Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
L.8ks: ^48:2^ Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.
L.8kt: ^48:3^ All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.
L.8kv: ^48:4^ My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding.
L.8kx: ^48:5^ I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.
L.8l0: ^48:6^ Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.
L.8l2: ^48:7^ They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,
L.8l4: ^48:8^ No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,
L.8l6: ^48:9^ Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.
L.8k3: ^48:11^ He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:
L.8k1: ^48:11^ And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.
L.8k6: ^48:12^ Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.
L.8k7: ^48:13^ And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.
L.8ka: ^48:14^ This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.
L.8ke: ^48:15^ They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.
L.8kb: ^48:15^ And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.
L.8kf: ^48:16^ But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.
L.8kh: ^48:17^ Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.
L.8kj: ^48:18^ For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.
L.8kl: ^48:19^ For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.
L.8kn: ^48:20^ He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.
L.8kq: ^48:21^ Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.
L.fdf: ^49:1^ Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * et vocávit terram,
L.8lr: ^49:1^ A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris ejus.
L.8m2: ^49:3^ Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
L.8m4: ^49:3^ Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet: * et in circúitu ejus tempéstas válida.
L.8m5: ^49:4^ Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
L.8m7: ^49:5^ Congregáte illi sanctos ejus: * qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia.
L.8ma: ^49:6^ Et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus: * quóniam Deus judex est.
L.8mb: ^49:7^ Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
L.8me: ^49:8^ Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
L.8mg: ^49:9^ Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
L.8l8: ^49:10^ Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * juménta in móntibus et boves.
L.8l9: ^49:11^ Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
L.8lc: ^49:12^ Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo ejus.
L.8ld: ^49:13^ Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
L.8lg: ^49:14^ Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
L.8li: ^49:15^ Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
L.8lk: ^49:16^ Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras justítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
L.8lm: ^49:17^ Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:
L.8lo: ^49:18^ Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
L.8lp: ^49:19^ Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
L.8lt: ^49:20^ Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.
L.8lv: ^49:21^ Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
L.8lx: ^49:22^ Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
L.8lz: ^49:23^ Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
L.fdg: ^49:1^ The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * and he hath called the earth.
L.8ls: ^49:1^ From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.
L.8m3: ^49:3^ God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.
L.8m1: ^49:3^ A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about.
L.8m6: ^49:4^ He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.
L.8m8: ^49:5^ Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.
L.8m9: ^49:6^ And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.
L.8mc: ^49:7^ Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.
L.8md: ^49:8^ I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.
L.8mf: ^49:9^ I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.
L.8l7: ^49:10^ For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.
L.8la: ^49:11^ I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.
L.8lb: ^49:12^ If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.
L.8le: ^49:13^ Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?
L.8lf: ^49:14^ Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.
L.8lh: ^49:15^ And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
L.8lj: ^49:16^ But to the sinner God hath said: * Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?
L.8ll: ^49:17^ Seeing thou hast hated discipline: * and hast cast my words behind thee.
L.8ln: ^49:18^ If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: * and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.
L.8lq: ^49:19^ Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, * and thy tongue framed deceits.
L.8lu: ^49:20^ Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son: * these things hast thou done, and I was silent.
L.8lw: ^49:21^ Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: * but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.
L.8ly: ^49:22^ Understand these things, you that forget God; * lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.
L.8m0: ^49:23^ The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: * and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.
L.8n2: ^51:3^ Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
L.8n5: ^51:4^ Tota die injustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
L.8n6: ^51:5^ Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
L.8n8: ^51:6^ Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
L.8na: ^51:7^ Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
L.8nd: ^51:8^ Vidébunt justi, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum:
L.8nf: ^51:9^ Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
L.8mz: ^51:10^ Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
L.8n0: ^51:11^ Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
L.8n3: ^51:3^ Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?
L.8n4: ^51:4^ All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.
L.8n7: ^51:5^ Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.
L.8n9: ^51:6^ Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.
L.8nb: ^51:7^ Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.
L.8nc: ^51:8^ The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:
L.8ne: ^51:9^ But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.
L.8my: ^51:10^ But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.
L.8n1: ^51:11^ I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.
L.gp2: ^Ant.^ Let the Saints rejoice in the Lord, * Alleluia.
L.eu2: ^1^ Festus ergo cum venísset in provínciam, post tríduum ascéndit Jerosólymam a Cæsaréa.
L.f45: ^2^ Adierúntque eum príncipes sacerdótum et primi Judæórum advérsus Paulum: et rogábant eum,
L.fc7: ^3^ Postulántes grátiam advérsus eum, ut jubéret perdúci eum in Jerúsalem, insídias tendéntes ut interfícerent eum in via.
L.ff8: ^4^ Festus autem respóndit servári Paulum in Cæsaréa: se autem matúrius profectúrum.
L.fja: ^5^ Qui ergo in vobis, ait, poténtes sunt, descendéntes simul, si quod est in viro crimen, accúsent eum.
L.9ky: ^℟.^ Ego sum vitis vera, et vos pálmites:
L.6ul: * Qui manet in me, et ego in eo, hic fert fructum multum, allelúja, allelúja.
L.9t4: ^℣.^ Sicut diléxit me Pater, et ego diléxi vos.
L.9ne: ^℟.^ Qui manet in me, et ego in eo, hic fert fructum multum, allelúja, allelúja.
L.euv: ^1^ Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days, he went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
L.f4n: ^2^ And the chief priests, and principal men of the Jews, went unto him against Paul: and they besought him,
L.fcc: ^3^ Requesting favour against him, that he would command him to be brought to Jerusalem, laying wait to kill him in the way.
L.fed: ^4^ But Festus answered: That Paul was kept in Caesarea, and that he himself would very shortly depart thither.
L.fj2: ^5^ Let them, therefore, saith he, among you that are able, go down with me, and accuse him, if there be any crime in the man.
L.9m1: ^℟.^ I am the True Vine, and ye are the branches;
L.6u9: * He that abideth in Me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit, alleluia, alleluia.
L.9q0: ^℣.^ As the Father hath loved Me, so have I loved you.
L.9ls: ^℟.^ He that abideth in Me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit, alleluia, alleluia.
L.fkr: ^6^ Demorátus autem inter eos dies non ámplius quam octo aut decem, descéndit Cæsaréam, et áltera die sedit pro tribunáli, et jussit Paulum addúci.
L.fou: ^7^ Qui cum perdúctus esset, circumstetérunt eum, qui ab Jerosólyma descénderant Judǽi, multas et graves causas obiciéntes, quas non póterant probáre:
L.fri: ^8^ Paulo ratiónem reddénte: Quóniam neque in legem Judæórum, neque in templum, neque in Cǽsarem quidquam peccávi.
L.jk4: ^℟.^ Surgens Jesus Dóminus noster, stans in médio discipulórum suórum, dixit:
L.a80: * Pax vobis, allelúja: gavísi sunt discípuli viso Dómino, allelúja.
L.kol: ^℣.^ Una ergo sabbatórum, cum fores essent clausæ, ubi erant discípuli congregáti, venit Jesus, et stetit in medio eórum, et dixit eis.
L.jfe: ^℟.^ Pax vobis, allelúja: gavísi sunt discípuli viso Dómino, allelúja.
L.fk0: ^6^ And having tarried among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and the next day he sat in the judgment seat; and commanded Paul to be brought.
L.fpc: ^7^ Who being brought, the Jews stood about him, who were come down from Jerusalem, objecting many and grievous causes, which they could not prove;
L.frh: ^8^ Paul making answer for himself: Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I offended in any thing.
L.iot: ^℟.^ After that our Lord Jesus was risen again, He came and stood in the midst of His disciples, and said unto them:
L.a81: * Peace be unto you, alleluia. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord, alleluia.
L.kln: ^℣.^ The first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled, came Jesus, and stood in the midst, and said unto them:
L.jff: ^℟.^ Peace be unto you, alleluia. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord, alleluia.
L.ftm: ^9^ Festus autem volens grátiam præstáre Judǽis, respóndens Paulo, dixit: Vis Jerosólymam ascéndere, et ibi de his judicári apud me?
L.eb4: ^10^ Dixit autem Paulus: Ad tribúnal Cǽsaris sto: ibi me opórtet judicári: Judǽis non nócui, sicut tu mélius nosti.
L.ef2: ^11^ Si enim nócui, aut dignum morte áliquid feci, non recúso mori: si vero nihil est eórum quæ hi accúsant me, nemo potest me illis donáre. Cǽsarem appéllo.
L.ehg: ^12^ Tunc Festus cum concílio locútus, respóndit: Cǽsarem appellásti? ad Cǽsarem ibis.
L.fsy: ^9^ But Festus, willing to show the Jews a pleasure, answering Paul, said: Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
L.ecn: ^10^ Then Paul said: I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no injury, as thou very well knowest.
L.ee6: ^11^ For if I have injured them, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die. But if there be none of these things whereof they accuse me, no man may deliver me to them: I appeal to Caesar.
L.ehc: ^12^ Then Festus having conferred with the council, answered: Hast thou appealed to Caesar? To Caesar shalt thou go.
L.c57: Incipit liber Apocalýpsis beáti Joánnis Apóstoli
L.eto: ^1^ Apocalýpsis Jesu Christi, quam dedit illi Deus palam fácere servis suis, quæ opórtet fíeri cito: et significávit, mittens per ángelum suum servo suo Joánni,
L.f6d: ^2^ Qui testimónium perhíbuit verbo Dei, et testimónium Jesu Christi, quæcúmque vidit.
L.fal: ^3^ Beátus qui legit, et audit verba prophetíæ hujus, et servat ea, quæ in ea scripta sunt: tempus enim prope est.
L.ffk: ^4^ Joánnes septem ecclésiis, quæ sunt in Asia. Grátia vobis, et pax ab eo, qui est, et qui erat, et qui ventúrus est: et a septem spirítibus qui in conspéctu throni ejus sunt:
L.fi8: ^5^ Et a Jesu Christo, qui est testis fidélis, primogénitus mortuórum, et princeps regum terræ, qui diléxit nos, et lavit nos a peccátis nostris in sánguine suo,
L.fl6: ^6^ Et fecit nos regnum, et sacerdótes Deo et Patri suo: ipsi glória et impérium in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
L.ixm: ^℟.^ Dignus es, Dómine, accípere librum, et aperíre signácula ejus, allelúja: quóniam occísus es, et redemísti nos Deo
L.k5g: ^℣.^ Fecísti enim nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdótium.
L.evc: ^1^ The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to make known to his servants the things which must shortly come to pass: and signified, sending by his angel to his servant John, who hath given testimony to the word of God, and the testimony of Jesus Christ, what things soever he hath seen.
L.fam: ^3^ Blessed is he, that readeth and heareth the words of this prophecy; and keepeth those things which are written in it; for the time is at hand.
L.ffj: ^4^ John to the seven churches which are in Asia. Grace be unto you and peace from him that is, and that was, and that is to come, and from the seven spirits which are before his throne,
L.fha: ^5^ And from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth, who hath loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood,
L.fjz: ^6^ And hath made us a kingdom, and priests to God and his Father, to him be glory and empire for ever and ever. Amen.
L.jp1: ^℟.^ Thou art worthy, O Lord, to take the book, and to open the seals thereof; alleluia: because thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God,
L.jw7: ^℣.^ And hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests.
L.fnl: ^7^ Ecce venit cum núbibus, et vidébit eum omnis óculus, et qui eum pupugérunt. Et plangent se super eum omnes tribus terræ. Etiam: amen.
L.fqg: ^8^ Ego sum alpha et ómega, princípium et finis, dicit Dóminus Deus: qui est, et qui erat, et qui ventúrus est, omnípotens.
L.ft7: ^9^ Ego Joánnes frater vester, et párticeps in tribulatióne, et regno, et patiéntia in Christo Jesu: fui in ínsula, quæ appellátur Patmos, propter verbum Dei, et testimónium Jesu:
L.ebk: ^10^ Fui in spíritu in domínica die, et audívi post me vocem magnam tamquam tubæ,
L.edo: ^11^ Dicéntis: Quod vides, scribe in libro: et mitte septem ecclésiis, quæ sunt in Asia, Epheso, et Smyrnæ, et Pérgamo, et Thyatíræ, et Sardis, et Philadelphíæ, et Laodicíæ.
L.iz1: ^℟.^ Ego sicut vitis fructificávi suavitátem odóris, allelúja:
L.abz: * Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis adimplémini, allelúja, allelúja.
L.kaa: ^℣.^ In me omnis grátia viæ et veritátis: in me omnes spes vitæ et virtútis.
L.jpo: ^℟.^ Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis adimplémini, allelúja, allelúja.
L.fnc: ^7^ Behold, he cometh with the clouds, and every eye shall see him, and they also that pierced him. And all the tribes of the earth shall bewail themselves because of him. Even so. Amen.
L.fr5: ^8^ I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, saith the Lord God, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.
L.ftu: ^9^ I John, your brother and your partner in tribulation, and in the kingdom, and patience in Christ Jesus, was in the island, which is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus.
L.ebo: ^10^ I was in the spirit on the Lord's day, and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,
L.ef0: ^11^ Saying: What thou seest, write in a book, and send to the seven churches which are in Asia, to Ephesus, and to Smyrna, and to Pergamus, and to Thyatira, and to Sardis, and to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.
L.isw: ^℟.^ As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour, alleluia.
L.a0l: * Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits, alleluia, alleluia.
L.kr2: ^℣.^ in me is all hope of life and of virtue.
L.ivr: ^℟.^ Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits, alleluia, alleluia.
L.egc: ^12^ Et convérsus sum ut vidérem vocem, quæ loquebátur mecum: et convérsus vidi septem candelábra áurea:
L.eii: ^13^ Et in médio septem candelabrórum aureórum, símilem Fílio hóminis vestítum podére, et præcínctum ad mamíllas zona áurea:

L.b9o: Diébus his sanctis resurrectióni Dómini dedicátis, quantum donánte ipso póssumus, de carnis resurrectióne tractémus. Hæc enim est fides nostra: hoc donum in Dómini nostri Jesu Christi nobis carne promíssum est, et in ipso præcéssit exémplum. Vóluit enim nobis, quod promísit in fine, non solum prænuntiáre, sed étiam demonstráre. Illi quidem qui tunc fuérunt, cum illum vidérent, et cum expavéscerent, et spíritum se vidére créderent, soliditátem córporis tenuérunt. Locútus est enim non solum verbis ad aures eórum, sed étiam spécie ad óculos eórum: parúmque erat se præbére cernéndum, nisi étiam offérret pertractándum atque palpándum.

L.d7s: Sermon from St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo)
L.ba8: During these Holy Days in commemoration of the Lord's resurrection, we purpose to preach, so far as he will empower us, the doctrine of the resurrection of the body. For this is the Faith, to wit: the gift of resurrection, which was bestowed upon the flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, is what is promised to us, for it was first made manifest in him that we might know what to hope for ourselves. What he hath thus promised would come to us at the last, he willed not only to foretell but to demonstrate. Those who were present at that time (even though they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed they had seen a spirit), handled him, and saw that a spirit would not have flesh and bones, such as they saw him to have. Thus he spake to them, not only in words which they could hear, but in a body which they could see; as if it had not been enough to shew himself to their sight, but must needs even offer himself to be touched and handled.
L.jeu: ^℟.^ One of the seven Angels talked with me, saying: Come hither, I will show thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.

L.ai1: Ait enim: Quid turbáti estis, et cogitatiónes ascéndunt in cor vestrum? Putavérunt enim se spíritum vidére. Quid turbáti estis, inquit, et cogitatiónes ascéndunt in cor vestrum? Vidéte manus meas, et pedes meos: palpáte, et vidéte: quia spíritus ossa et carnem non habet, sicut me vidétis habére. Contra istam evidéntiam disputábant hómines. Quid enim áliud fácerent hómines, qui ea, quæ sunt hóminum, sápiunt, quam sic disputáre de Deo contra Deum? Ille enim Deus est, isti hómines sunt. Sed Deus novit cogitatiónes hóminum, quóniam vanæ sunt.
L.iti: ^℟.^ Audívi vocem in cælo Angelórum multórum dicéntium:
L.abt: * Timéte Dóminum, et date claritátem illi, et adoráte eum, qui fecit cælum et terram, mare et fontes aquárum, allelúja, allelúja.

L.jpc: ^℟.^ Timéte Dóminum, et date claritátem illi, et adoráte eum, qui fecit cælum et terram, mare et fontes aquárum, allelúja, allelúja.
L.bh6: For he said: Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? For they supposed that they had seen a spirit. Therefore he added: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; handle me and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have. Of course, men have disputed this evidence; for what else could men do, seeing that they are wise only according to man's wisdom, which thus permitteth them to dispute concerning God in spite of what God hath shewn them of himself. He is God, they are men. But God knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are but vain.
L.j6s: ^℟.^ I heard in heaven the voice of many Angels, saying
L.a3u: * Fear the Lord, and give glory to Him, and worship Him That made heaven and earth, the sea, and the fountains of waters. Alleluia, Alleluia.
L.k99: ^℣.^ I saw a strong Angel of God fly through the midst of heaven, crying with a loud voice and saying
L.j2s: ^℟.^ Fear the Lord, and give glory to Him, and worship Him That made heaven and earth, the sea, and the fountains of waters. Alleluia, Alleluia.
L.bxd: In hómine carnáli tota régula intelligéndi est consuetúdo cernéndi. Quod solent vidére, credunt: quod non solent, non credunt. Præter consuetúdinem facit Deus mirácula, quia Deus est. Majóra quidem mirácula sunt, tot quotídie hómines nasci, qui non erant, quam paucos resurrexísse, qui erant: et tamen ista mirácula non consideratióne comprehénsa sunt, sed assiduitáte viluérunt. Resurréxit Christus: absolúta est res. Corpus erat, caro erat: pepéndit in cruce, emísit ánimam, pósita est caro in sepúlcro. Exhíbuit illam vivam, qui vivébat in illa. Quare mirámur? quare non crédimus? Deus est, qui fecit.
L.jrh: ^℟.^ Véniens a Líbano quam pulchra facta est, allelúja:
L.a2m: * Et odor vestimentórum ejus super ómnia arómata, allelúja, allelúja.
L.k5b: ^℣.^ Favus distíllans lábia ejus, mel et lac sub lingua ejus.

L.dnh: To carnal men, the one rule of understanding is his ordinary experience; seeing is believing. What men are accustomed to see, that they credit; what they are not accustomed to see, that they deem incredible. But God often worketh wonders (that is, things contrary to what we are accustomed), because he is God. Every day many men are born that previously had no existence at all; and this is a greater miracle than that a few, who did exist, have been raised from the dead. Yet this wonder is not recognized as such; on the contrary, it is disregarded because man is accustomed to it. Christ rose again from the dead; that is a fact. He had a body: he took flesh, he hung upon the cross, he gave up the ghost; his flesh was laid in the tomb. After that, he shewed his flesh as alive again, he lived again the flesh. Why wonder, why deny it? God wrought this.

L.bzg: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Módicum, et jam non vidébitis me; et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me: quia vado ad Patrem. Et réliqua.
L.cii: Módicum est hoc totum spátium, quo præsens pérvolat sǽculum. Unde dicit idem ipse Evangelísta in Epístola sua: Novíssima hora est. Ideo namque áddidit: Quia vado ad Patrem: quod ad priórem senténtiam referéndum est, ubi ait: Módicum et jam non vidébitis me: non ad posteriórem, ubi ait: Et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me. Eúndo quippe ad Patrem, factúrus erat ut eum non vidérent. Ac per hoc non ídeo dictum est, quia fúerat moritúrus, et donec resúrgeret, ab eórum aspéctibus recessúrus: sed quod esset itúrus ad Patrem, quod fecit posteáquam resurréxit, et cum eis per quadragínta dies conversátus, ascéndit in cælum.
L.iwy: ^℟.^ Decantábat pópulus Israël, allelúja: et univérsa multitúdo Jacob canébat legítime:
L.a1n: * Et David cum cantóribus cítharam percutiébat in domo Dómini, et laudes Deo canébat, allelúja, allelúja.
L.kiq: ^℣.^ Sanctificáti sunt ergo sacerdótes et levítæ: et univérsus Israël deducébat arcam fœ́deris Dómini in júbilo.
L.izl: ^℟.^ Et David cum cantóribus cítharam percutiébat in domo Dómini, et laudes Deo canébat, allelúja, allelúja.
L.apb: At that time, Jesus said to his disciples: A little while, and now you shall not see me; and again a little while, and you shall see me: because I go to the Father. And so on.
L.dla: This little while is the whole duration of this present world. In the same sense this same Evangelist saith in his Epistle ^ii. 18^: It is the last time. The words, because I go to the Father, refer to the first clause of the text, namely, A little while and ye shall not see Me, and not to the latter clause, that is, and again a little while, and ye shall see Me. By His going to the Father He was about to bring it to pass that they should see Him no more. And thus it was that He said, not that He was about to die, and that after His death they should not see Him until He rose again, but that He was going to the Father, which He did when, after that He was risen again and had manifested Himself to them for forty days, He ascended up into heaven.
L.jmv: ^℟.^ The people of Israel sung: Alleluia, and all the multitude of Jacob sung in measure.
L.9xu: * And David was with the singers, (and) played upon an harp in the house of the Lord, and sung praises unto God. Alleluia, Alleluia.

L.bve: Illis ergo ait: Módicum, et jam non vidébitis me; qui eum corporáliter tunc vidébant: quia itúrus erat ad Patrem, et eum deínceps mortálem visúri non erant, qualem, cum ista loquerétur, vidébant. Quod vero áddidit: Et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me: univérsæ promísit Ecclésiæ, sicut univérsæ promísit: Ecce ego vobíscum sum usque ad consummatiónem sǽculi. Non tardat Dóminus promíssum. Módicum et vidébimus eum: ubi jam nihil rogémus, nihil interrogémus, quia nihil desiderándum remanébit, nihil quæréndum latébit.
L.kdo: ^℣.^ Mundus autem gaudébit, vos vero contristabímini, sed tristítia vestra.
L.ax6: But now, to them which were looking on Him in the Body, He saith: A little while, and ye shall not see Me, a little while, and they who now saw Him clad in a dying nature, should see Him so no more, because He was about to go to the Father. But He saith: And again a little while, and ye shall see Me, and these words are a promise to the Universal Church, just as are those others: Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world ^Matth. xxviii. 20.^ Our Lord delayeth not His promised coming. Again a little while, and we shall see Him. We shall see Him. And, O, when we shall see Him, then we shall beg, we shall ask no more; for no desire will be unsatisfied, and no riddle unsolved.
L.a9t: * Shall be turned into joy. Alleluia.
L.kmb: ^℣.^ The world shall rejoice; and you shall be made sorrowful: but your sorrow
L.jj6: ^℟.^ Shall be turned into joy. Alleluia.
L.brx: Hoc módicum longum nobis vidétur, quóniam adhuc ágitur; cum finítum fúerit, tunc sentiémus quam módicum fúerit. Non ergo sit gáudium nostrum quale habet mundus, de quo dictum est: Mundus autem gaudébit. Nec tamen in hujus desidérii parturitióne sine gáudio tristes simus: sed, sicut ait Apóstolus: Spe gaudéntes: In tribulatióne patiéntes: quia et ipsa partúriens, cui comparáti sumus, plus gaudet de mox futúra prole, quam tristis est de præsénti dolóre. Sed hujus sermónis iste sit finis: habent enim quæstiónem molestíssimam, quæ sequúntur: nec brevitáte coarctánda sunt, ut possint commódius, si Dóminus volúerit, explicári.
L.dlb: This little while seemeth a very long while to us now, while as it is still going on, but when it is over we shall feel indeed how truly it is but a little while. Therefore, may our rejoicing never be like the rejoicing of that world whereof it is said: The world shall rejoice. A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, and yet, while hitherto our gladness is still coming to the birth through throes of sorrow, let us not be altogether sorrowful, but, as the Apostle hath it ^Rom. xii. 12^: Rejoicing in hope: patient in tribulation. A woman, when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world. And so will it be with us. And with that let me end my discourse. The next passage is one of extreme difficulty; nor is it possible to treat it briefly, if, (with the will of God,) it is to be treated satisfactorily.

L.8ab: ^30:23^ But I said in the excess of my mind: * I am cast away from before thy eyes.
L.8ad: ^30:23^ Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, * when I cried to thee.
L.8ag: ^30:24^ O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.
L.8ah: ^30:25^ Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.
L.8bo: ^34:1^ Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, * expúgna impugnántes me.
L.8c9: ^34:2^ Apprehénde arma et scutum: * et exsúrge in adjutórium mihi.
L.8cc: ^34:3^ Effúnde frámeam, et conclúde advérsus eos, qui persequúntur me: * dic ánimæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.
L.8ce: ^34:4^ Confundántur et revereántur, * quæréntes ánimam meam.
L.8cd: ^34:4^ Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur * cogitántes mihi mala.
L.8ch: ^34:5^ Fiant tamquam pulvis ante fáciem venti: * et Ángelus Dómini coárctans eos.
L.8cj: ^34:6^ Fiat via illórum ténebræ et lúbricum: * et Ángelus Dómini pérsequens eos.
L.8cm: ^34:7^ Quóniam gratis abscondérunt mihi intéritum láquei sui: * supervácue exprobravérunt ánimam meam.
L.8co: ^34:8^ Véniat illi láqueus, quem ignórat: et cáptio, quam abscóndit, apprehéndat eum: * et in láqueum cadat in ipsum.
L.8cq: ^34:9^ Ánima autem mea exsultábit in Dómino: * et delectábitur super salutári suo.
L.8b2: ^34:10^ Ómnia ossa mea dicent: * Dómine, quis símilis tibi?
L.8b0: ^34:10^ Erípiens ínopem de manu fortiórum ejus: * egénum et páuperem a diripiéntibus eum.
L.8b3: ^34:11^ Surgéntes testes iníqui, * quæ ignorábam interrogábant me.
L.8b5: ^34:12^ Retribuébant mihi mala pro bonis: * sterilitátem ánimæ meæ.
L.8b8: ^34:13^ Ego autem cum mihi molésti essent, * induébar cilício.
L.8b9: ^34:13^ Humiliábam in jejúnio ánimam meam: * et orátio mea in sinu meo convertétur.
L.8bc: ^34:14^ Quasi próximum, et quasi fratrem nostrum, sic complacébam: * quasi lugens et contristátus, sic humiliábar.
L.8be: ^34:15^ Et advérsum me lætáti sunt, et convenérunt: * congregáta sunt super me flagélla, et ignorávi.
L.8bf: ^34:16^ Dissipáti sunt, nec compúncti, tentavérunt me, subsannavérunt me subsannatióne: * frenduérunt super me déntibus suis.
L.8bh: ^34:17^ Dómine, quando respícies? * restítue ánimam meam a malignitáte eórum, a leónibus únicam meam.
L.8bj: ^34:18^ Confitébor tibi in ecclésia magna, * in pópulo gravi laudábo te.
L.8bm: ^34:19^ Non supergáudeant mihi qui adversántur mihi iníque: * qui odérunt me gratis et ánnuunt óculis.
L.8bq: ^34:20^ Quóniam mihi quidem pacífice loquebántur: * et in iracúndia terræ loquéntes, dolos cogitábant.
L.8bs: ^34:21^ Et dilatavérunt super me os suum: * dixérunt: Euge, euge, vidérunt óculi nostri.
L.8bu: ^34:22^ Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas: * Dómine, ne discédas a me.
L.8bw: ^34:23^ Exsúrge et inténde judício meo: * Deus meus, et Dóminus meus in causam meam.
L.8by: ^34:24^ Júdica me secúndum justítiam tuam, Dómine, Deus meus, * et non supergáudeant mihi.
L.8c0: ^34:25^ Non dicant in córdibus suis: Euge, euge, ánimæ nostræ: * nec dicant: Devorávimus eum.
L.8c1: ^34:26^ Erubéscant et revereántur simul, * qui gratulántur malis meis.
L.8c2: ^34:26^ Induántur confusióne et reveréntia * qui magna loquúntur super me.
L.8c5: ^34:27^ Exsúltent et læténtur qui volunt justítiam meam: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus qui volunt pacem servi ejus.
L.8c8: ^34:28^ Et lingua mea meditábitur justítiam tuam, * tota die laudem tuam.
L.8bn: ^34:1^ Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: * overthrow them that fight against me.
L.8ca: ^34:2^ Take hold of arms and shield: * and rise up to help me.
L.8cb: ^34:3^ Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: * say to my soul: I am thy salvation.
L.8cf: ^34:4^ Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek after my soul.
L.8cg: ^34:4^ Let them be turned back and be confounded * that devise against me.
L.8ci: ^34:5^ Let them become as dust before the wind: * and let the Angel of the Lord straiten them.
L.8ck: ^34:6^ Let their way become dark and slippery; * and let the Angel of the Lord pursue them.
L.8cl: ^34:7^ For without cause they have hidden their net for me unto destruction: * without cause they have upbraided my soul.
L.8cn: ^34:8^ Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him: and let the net which he hath hidden catch him: * and into that very snare let them fall.
L.8cp: ^34:9^ But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord; * and shall be delighted in his salvation.
L.8az: ^34:10^ All my bones shall say: * Lord, who is like to thee?
L.8b1: ^34:10^ Who deliverest the poor from the hand of them that are stronger than he; * the needy and the poor from them that strip him.
L.8b4: ^34:11^ Unjust witnesses rising up * have asked me things I knew not.
L.8b6: ^34:12^ They repaid me evil for good: * to the depriving me of my soul.
L.8b7: ^34:13^ But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, * I was clothed with haircloth.
L.8ba: ^34:13^ I humbled my soul with fasting; * and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.
L.8bb: ^34:14^ As a neighbour and as an own brother, so did I please: * as one mourning and sorrowful so was I humbled.
L.8bd: ^34:15^ But they rejoiced against me, and came together: * scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not.
L.8bg: ^34:16^ They were separated, and repented not: they tempted me, they scoffed at me with scorn: * they gnashed upon me with their teeth.
L.8bi: ^34:17^ Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? * rescue thou my soul from their malice: my only one from the lions.
L.8bk: ^34:18^ I will give thanks to thee in a great church; * I will praise thee in a strong people.
L.8bl: ^34:19^ Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: * who have hated me without cause, and wink with the eyes.
L.8bp: ^34:20^ For they spoke indeed peaceably to me; * and speaking in the anger of the earth they devised guile.
L.8br: ^34:21^ And they opened their mouth wide against me; * they said: Well done, well done, our eyes have seen it.
L.8bt: ^34:22^ Thou hast seen, O Lord, be not thou silent: * O Lord, depart not from me.
L.8bv: ^34:23^ Arise, and be attentive to my judgment: * to my cause, my God, and my Lord.
L.8bx: ^34:24^ Judge me, O Lord my God according to thy justice, * and let them not rejoice over me.
L.8bz: ^34:25^ Let them not say in their hearts: It is well, it is well, to our mind: * neither let them say: We have swallowed him up.
L.8c4: ^34:26^ Let them blush: and be ashamed together, * who rejoice at my evils.
L.8c3: ^34:26^ Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, * who speak great things against me.
L.8c6: ^34:27^ Let them rejoice and be glad, who are well pleased with my justice, * and let them say always: The Lord be magnified, who delights in the peace of his servant.
L.8c7: ^34:28^ And my tongue shall meditate thy justice, * thy praise all the day long.
L.8d1: ^35:2^ Dixit injústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos ejus.
L.8d4: ^35:3^ Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu ejus: * ut inveniátur iníquitas ejus ad ódium.
L.8d6: ^35:4^ Verba oris ejus iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.
L.8d8: ^35:5^ Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.
L.8d9: ^35:6^ Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
L.8dc: ^35:7^ Justítia tua sicut montes Dei: * judícia tua abýssus multa.
L.8db: ^35:7^ Hómines, et juménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
L.8dg: ^35:8^ Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
L.8dh: ^35:9^ Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
L.8cu: ^35:10^ Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
L.8cw: ^35:11^ Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et justítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
L.8cy: ^35:12^ Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
L.8cz: ^35:13^ Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
L.8d2: ^35:2^ The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: * there is no fear of God before his eyes.
L.8d3: ^35:3^ For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, * that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.
L.8d5: ^35:4^ The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: * he would not understand that he might do well.
L.8d7: ^35:5^ He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.
L.8da: ^35:6^ O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.
L.8de: ^35:7^ Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.
L.8dd: ^35:7^ Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!
L.8df: ^35:8^ But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.
L.8di: ^35:9^ They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.
L.8ct: ^35:10^ For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.
L.8cv: ^35:11^ Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.
L.8cx: ^35:12^ Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.
L.8d0: ^35:13^ There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.
L.8e9: ^36:1^ Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
L.8ex: ^36:2^ Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
L.8fi: ^36:3^ Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis ejus.
L.8fm: ^36:4^ Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
L.8fp: ^36:5^ Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
L.8fr: ^36:6^ Et edúcet quasi lumen justítiam tuam: et judícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
L.8ft: ^36:7^ Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte injustítias.
L.8fv: ^36:8^ Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
L.8fx: ^36:9^ Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
L.8dm: ^36:10^ Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum ejus et non invénies.
L.8dp: ^36:11^ Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
L.8dq: ^36:12^ Observábit peccátor justum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
L.8dt: ^36:13^ Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies ejus.
L.8du: ^36:14^ Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
L.8dx: ^36:14^ Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
L.8dy: ^36:15^ Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
L.8e1: ^36:16^ Mélius est módicum justo, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
L.8e3: ^36:17^ Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem justos Dóminus.
L.8e4: ^36:18^ Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
L.8e6: ^36:19^ Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
L.8eb: ^36:20^ Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
L.8ec: ^36:21^ Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * justus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
L.8ef: ^36:22^ Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
L.8eg: ^36:23^ Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam ejus volet.
L.8ei: ^36:24^ Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
L.8el: ^36:25^ Júnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi justum derelíctum, nec semen ejus quærens panem.
L.8en: ^36:26^ Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
L.8ep: ^36:27^ Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
L.8es: ^36:28^ Quia Dóminus amat judícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
L.8er: ^36:28^ Injústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
L.8ev: ^36:29^ Justi autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
L.8ey: ^36:30^ Os justi meditábitur sapiéntiam, * et lingua ejus loquétur judícium.
L.8f0: ^36:31^ Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus, * et non supplantabúntur gressus ejus.
L.8f2: ^36:32^ Consíderat peccátor justum: * et quærit mortificáre eum.
L.8f5: ^36:33^ Dóminus autem non derelínquet eum in mánibus ejus: * nec damnábit eum, cum judicábitur illi.
L.8f7: ^36:34^ Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam ejus: et exaltábit te ut hereditáte cápias terram: * cum períerint peccatóres vidébis.
L.8f9: ^36:35^ Vidi ímpium superexaltátum, * et elevátum sicut cedros Líbani.
L.8fb: ^36:36^ Et transívi, et ecce non erat: * et quæsívi eum, et non est invéntus locus ejus.
L.8fc: ^36:37^ Custódi innocéntiam, et vide æquitátem: * quóniam sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico.
L.8ff: ^36:38^ Injústi autem disperíbunt simul: * relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt.
L.8fh: ^36:39^ Salus autem justórum a Dómino: * et protéctor eórum in témpore tribulatiónis.
L.8fl: ^36:40^ Et adjuvábit eos Dóminus et liberábit eos: * et éruet eos a peccatóribus, et salvábit eos: quia speravérunt in eo.
L.8e8: ^36:1^ Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.
L.8ew: ^36:2^ For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.
L.8fj: ^36:3^ Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.
L.8fn: ^36:4^ Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
L.8fo: ^36:5^ Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.
L.8fq: ^36:6^ And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.
L.8fs: ^36:7^ Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.
L.8fu: ^36:8^ Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.
L.8fw: ^36:9^ For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.
L.8dn: ^36:10^ For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.
L.8do: ^36:11^ But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.
L.8dr: ^36:12^ The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.
L.8ds: ^36:13^ But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.
L.8dv: ^36:14^ The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.
L.8dw: ^36:14^ To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.
L.8dz: ^36:15^ Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.
L.8e0: ^36:16^ Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.
L.8e2: ^36:17^ For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
L.8e5: ^36:18^ The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.
L.8e7: ^36:19^ They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.
L.8ea: ^36:20^ And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, * shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.
L.8ed: ^36:21^ The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; * but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.
L.8ee: ^36:22^ For such as bless him shall inherit the land: * but such as curse him shall perish.
L.8eh: ^36:23^ With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, * and he shall like well his way.
L.8ej: ^36:24^ When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, * for the Lord putteth his hand under him.
L.8ek: ^36:25^ I have been young, and now am old; * and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.
L.8em: ^36:26^ He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; * and his seed shall be in blessing.
L.8eo: ^36:27^ Decline from evil and do good, * and dwell for ever and ever.
L.8eq: ^36:28^ For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: * they shall be preserved for ever.
L.8et: ^36:28^ The unjust shall be punished, * and the seed of the wicked shall perish.
L.8eu: ^36:29^ But the just shall inherit the land, * and shall dwell therein for evermore.
L.8ez: ^36:30^ The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: * and his tongue shall speak judgment.
L.8f1: ^36:31^ The law of his God is in his heart, * and his steps shall not be supplanted.
L.8f3: ^36:32^ The wicked watcheth the just man, * and seeketh to put him to death.
L.8f4: ^36:33^ But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; * nor condemn him when he shall be judged.
L.8f6: ^36:34^ Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: * when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.
L.8f8: ^36:35^ I have seen the wicked highly exalted, * and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.
L.8fa: ^36:36^ And I passed by, and lo, he was not: * and I sought him and his place was not found.
L.8fd: ^36:37^ Keep innocence, and behold justice: * for there are remnants for the peaceable man.
L.8fe: ^36:38^ But the unjust shall be destroyed together: * the remnants of the wicked shall perish.
L.8fg: ^36:39^ But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in the time of trouble.
L.8fk: ^36:40^ And the Lord will help them and deliver them: * and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.
L.etx: ^1^ Et osténdit mihi flúvium aquæ vitæ, spléndidum tamquam crystállum, procedéntem de sede Dei et Agni.
L.f5z: ^2^ In médio platéæ ejus, et ex utráque parte flúminis, lignum vitæ, áfferens fructus duódecim per menses síngulos, reddens fructum suum et fólia ligni ad sanitátem géntium.
L.fba: ^3^ Et omne maledíctum non erit ámplius: sed sedes Dei et Agni in illa erunt, et servi ejus sérvient illi.
L.ff4: ^4^ Et vidébunt fáciem ejus: et nomen ejus in fróntibus eórum.
L.fif: ^5^ Et nox ultra non erit: et non egébunt lúmine lucérnæ, neque lúmine solis, quóniam Dóminus Deus illuminábit illos, et regnábunt in sǽcula sæculórum.
L.fl4: ^6^ Et dixit mihi: Hæc verba fidelíssima sunt, et vera. Et Dóminus Deus spirítuum prophetárum misit ángelum suum osténdere servis suis quæ opórtet fíeri cito.
L.fns: ^7^ Et ecce vénio velóciter. Beátus, qui custódit verba prophetíæ libri hujus.
L.a91: * Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti, allelúja.
L.jha: ^℟.^ Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulisti, allelúja.
L.etg: ^1^ And he showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
L.f61: ^2^ In the midst of the street thereof, and on both sides of the river, was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits, yielding its fruits every month, and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
L.faa: ^3^ And there shall be no curse any more; but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it, and his servants shall serve him.
L.fe7: ^4^ And they shall see his face: and his name shall be on their foreheads.
L.fhe: ^5^ And night shall be no more: and they shall not need the light of the lamp, nor the light of the sun, because the Lord God shall enlighten them, and they shall reign for ever and ever.
L.fk1: ^6^ And he said to me: These words are most faithful and true. And the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show his servants the things which must be done shortly.
L.fn7: ^7^ And, Behold I come quickly. Blessed is he that keepeth the words of the prophecy of this book.
L.a4n: * For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain, alleluia.
L.j3m: ^℟.^ For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain, alleluia.
L.fqp: ^8^ Et ego Joánnes, qui audívi, et vidi hæc. Et postquam audíssem, et vidíssem, cécidi ut adorárem ante pedes ángeli, qui mihi hæc ostendébat:
L.ftf: ^9^ Et dixit mihi: Vide ne féceris: consérvus enim tuus sum, et fratrum tuórum prophetárum, et eórum qui servant verba prophetíæ libri hujus: Deum adóra.
L.eb8: ^10^ Et dicit mihi: Ne signáveris verba prophetíæ libri hujus: tempus enim prope est.
L.eey: ^11^ Qui nocet, nóceat adhuc: et qui in sórdibus est, sordéscat adhuc: et qui justus est, justificétur adhuc: et sanctus, sanctificétur adhuc.
L.ega: ^12^ Ecce vénio cito, et merces mea mecum est, réddere unicuíque secúndum ópera sua.

Quam vero Christus eum familiáriter adhibéret, illud fácile declárat, quod gentíles Salvatórem vidére cupiéntes, ad Philíppum accessérunt; et Dóminus, cum in solitúdine hóminum multitúdinem páscere vellet, sic Philíppum affátus est: Unde emémus panes, ut mandúcent hi? L.o7l: James, surnamed the Just, the brother of our Lord Jesus Christ, was a Nazarite from the womb. During his whole life he never drank wine or strong drink, never ate meat, never shaved, and never took a bath. He was the only man who was allowed to go into the Holy of Holies. His raiment was always linen. So continually did he kneel in prayer, that the skin of his knees became horny, like a camel’s knees. After Christ was ascended, the Apostles made James Bishop of Jerusalem and even the Prince of the Apostles gave special intelligence to him after that he was delivered from prison by an angel. When in the Council of Jerusalem certain questions were mooted touching the law and circumcision, James, following the opinion of Peter, addressed a discourse to the brethren, wherein he proved the call of the Gentiles, and commanded letters to be sent to such brethren as were absent, that they might take heed not to lay upon the Gentiles the yoke of the Law of Moses. It is of him that the Apostle Paul saith, writing to the Galatians: “Other of the Apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.”

L.m0s: Athanasius Alexandrinus, catholicæ religiónis propugnator acerrimus, ab Alexandro episcopo Alexandrino diaconus factus est, in cujus locum successit. Quem étiam antea secutus fuerat ad Nicænum Concílium; ubi cum Aríi impietátem repressísset, tantum ódium Arianórum suscépit, ut ex eo témpore ei insidias moliri numquam destiterint. Nam coacto ad Tyrum concílio magna ex parte Arianórum episcopórum, subornarunt muliérculam, quæ accusaret Athansium, quod hospítio acceptus sibi stuprum per vim intulísset. Introductus ígitur est Athanasius, et una cum eo Timótheus presbyter; qui simulans se esse Athanasium, Ego ne, inquit, mulier, apud te sum diversatus? ego te violávi? Cui illa petulanter: Tu mihi vim attulísti; idque jurejurando affirmans, judicum fidem obtestabátur, ut tantum flagitium vindicárent. Qua cógnita fraude, rejecta est mulíeris impudéntia.

L.qp7: The great Athanasius, the greatest soldier that the Catholic Religion hath perhaps ever had, was an Alexandrian. He was ordained Deacon by Alexander, ^in the year 326,^ Bishop of that city, whom he afterwards succeeded. ^In 325^ he had followed Alexander to the Council of Nicea, where he wrestled triumphantly against the blasphemy of Arius. For this reason he was honoured with so much of their hatred by the Arians, that their vindictiveness never forsook him from that time forward. ^In the year 335,^ they called together a Council at Tyre, composed for the most part of Arian Bishops, where they suborned a wretched woman to charge Athanasius with having raped her when she had received him as a guest into her house. Athanasius therefore came into the assembly, and with him a certain priest whose name was Timothy. This Timothy arose as though he were Athanasius, and asked her, saying Woman, was it I that was thy guest was it I that raped thee She cried out indignantly Yea, thou it was that didst rape me, the which she attested with an oath, and called on the honour of the judges to punish such iniquity. Upon this discovery of her perjury, they drave the shameless woman from their presence.

L.lv0: Arsénium quoque episcopum ab Athanasio interfectum Ariáni pervulgarunt; quem dum occulte détinent, manum mórtui déferunt in judícium, ab Athanasio ad usum mágicæ artis Arsenio amputatam criminantes. At Arsenius noctu aufúgiens, cum se in conspectu totius concilii statuísset, Athanasii inimicórum impudentíssimum scelus apéruit. Quod illi nihilóminus mágicis artibus Athanasii tribuéntes, vitæ ejus insidiari non desistebant. Quam ob rem in exsílium actus, in Gállia apud Tréviros exsulávit. Gravibus deinceps ac diuturnis sub Constantio imperatóre, Arianórum fautore, tempestátibus jactátus et incredibiles calamitátes perpéssus, magnam orbis terræ partem peragrávit; ac sæpe e sua ecclésia ejéctus, sæpe étiam in eamdem et Julii, Romani Pontificis, auctoritate, et Constántis imperatóris, Constantii fratris, patrocinio, decretis quoque concilii Sardicénsis ac Jerosolymitani, restitútus est, Ariánis interea illi semper infestis; quorum pertinacem iram, et summum vitæ discrimen fúgiens, in sicca cisterna quinque annis se ábdidit, ejus rei tantum conscio quodam Athanasii amico, qui eum clam sustentabat.
L.qmf: The Arians also accused Athanasius of having murdered the (schismatic) Bishop Arsenius. This Arsenius they kept shut up, and brought into the court a dead man's hand, which they declared had been his, and had been cut off by Athanasius to use in sorcery. But Arsenius escaped in the night, and when he appeared before all the Council whole and sound, the brazen-faced crime of the enemies of Athanasius was exposed. This appearance nevertheless they attributed to Athanasius being a warlock, and persisted still in their attack on him. He was driven into exile, and banished to Treves in Gaul. Thenceforth, under authority of the Emperor Constantius, that abettor of Arians, he was hunted to and fro with unceasing persecutions. He suffered hardships which it is difficult to believe. He was sent wandering all about the Roman world. He was twice more thrust out of his See, and again restored through the authority of Pope Julius of Rome, and with the protection of the Emperor Constans, the brother of Constantius, by decrees of the Councils of Sardica and of Jerusalem. The vindictiveness of the Arians never let him alone. In his third exile so great was the danger of his life from the pursuit of their undying hatred, that he had to lie hid for five years in a dry cistern, unknown to all men, save one of his friends who brought him food.
L.mgc: Constantio mortuo, cum Julianus Apóstata, qui ei in imperio successit, éxsules episcopos ad suas ecclésias redire permisísset, Athanasius Alexandríam reversus, summo honóre exceptus est. Sed non multo post, iísdem Ariánis impelléntibus, a Juliáno exagitatus, rursus discedere cogitur. Cumque ab ejus satellítibus ad necem conquirerétur, qua fugiebat navícula conversa in contrariam flúminis partem, iis qui se insequebántur, ex industria occurrit; et quæréntibus quantum inde abesset Athanasius, respóndit eum non longe abesse: ítaque illos contrárium tenéntes cursum effugit, atque Alexandríam rédiens, ibidem usque ad Juliáni óbitum occultus permansit. Qui paulo post, Alexandríæ alia exorta tempestáte, quatuor menses in paterno sepúlcro delituit. Ac denique ex tot tantisque periculis divinitus ereptus, Alexandríæ mórtuus est in suo léctulo, sub Valénte: cujus vita et mors magnis nobilitáta est miraculis. Multa pie et ad illustrándum catholicam fidem præcláre scripsit, sexque et quadragínta annos in summa témporum varietáte Alexandrinam ecclésiam sanctíssime gubernávit.

L.lnf: After the death of Constantius, Julian the Apostate, who succeeded him, allowed every sort of Bishop who had been banished to return to their own Churches. Athanasius therefore returned to Alexandria, and was received with profound reverence. But it was not long before the same Arians got Julian to hunt him down again, and again it behoved him to fly. A band of soldiers were sent in pursuit of him to kill him, and as he fled up the Nile, their boat pressed hard on his. Athanasius, before they were yet in sight, had his own boat turned round, and went down the stream to meet them. As the vessels passed one another the murderers called out to ask if they knew where Athanasius was, and the servant of God himself cried to them in answer, Ye are close to him! whereupon they redoubled their exertions to ascend the stream, and Athanasius went peacefully down to Alexandria, and found means of concealment till the death of Julian. Yet once again he had to fly from another persecution at Alexandria, and in this his fifth and last exile he hid himself for four months in his own father's sepulchre. From all these so many and so great dangers did God deliver him, and at last he died in his own bed at Alexandria, ^upon the 2nd day of May, in the year of salvation 373,^ in the reign of Valens. He wrote much that is both godly and luminous in explaining the Catholic Faith, and governed the Church of Alexandria in great holiness, amid all changes of weather, for six and forty years.
